anonymous redactorial voice of this unit
88b.7 רבי זירא; 89a.11 רבי זעירא ואיתימא רבה בר ירמיה
the baraita Rav Rechumi cites: שופר / לולב של עבודה זרה לא יתקע / לא יטול

props.gloss_en: 'and cover it': might one cover it with stones or overturn a vessel on it? the verse says 'with earth'

whence to include fine manure, fine sand, crushed stones, crushed potsherd, fine flax-chaff, fine carpenters' sawdust, lime, potsherd, and a brick or stopper one crushed? the verse says 'and cover it'
might I include even coarse manure, coarse sand, metal filings, an uncrushed brick or stopper, flour, bran and coarse bran? the verse says 'with earth'
why include these and exclude those? since the verse included and excluded, I include those that are a species of earth and exclude those that are not
what is a species of earth is fit for covering; what is not, is excluded
say: 'and cover it' is a generalisation and 'earth' a detail; the generalisation holds only the detail -- earth yes, anything else no
Rav Mari: because it is a generalisation that needs its detail
and any generalisation that needs its detail is not expounded as generalisation-and-detail
Rav Nachman bar Rav Chisda expounded: one covers only with something one sows in and it sprouts
one travelling in the desert with no ashes to cover -- grinds a gold dinar and covers
one travelling on a ship with no earth to cover -- burns his garment and covers
ash is called 'earth' (afar)
R' Zeira: 'and it has dust of gold' (Job 28:6) -- the source for the ground gold dinar
Beit Shammai: one covers only with earth
Beit Hillel's verse: 'and they shall take for the impure from the earth of the burning' (Num 19:17)
Beit Shammai: ash is called 'earth of burning'; it is not called plain 'earth'
they added to them coal-dust, kohl and chisel-shavings
and some say: also arsenic
in reward for Abraham's 'I am dust and ashes' (Gen 18:27), his children merited two mitzvot: the ashes of the heifer and the dust of the sota
there [the earth of covering] is a mitzva-enabler; there is no benefit in it
in reward for Abraham's 'from a thread' (Gen 14:23), his children merited the thread of techelet
...and for 'to a shoe-strap', the strap of tefillin
R' Eliezer the Great: 'all the peoples of the earth shall see that the name of the Lord is called upon you' (Deut 28:10) -- these are the head-tefillin
R' Meir: why is techelet singled out from all colours? techelet resembles the sea, the sea the sky, the sky sapphire, and sapphire the Throne of Glory (Ex 24:10; Ezek 1:26)
R' Abba: hard is eaten theft, for even the wholly righteous cannot return it
as it says: 'except only what the young men have eaten' (Gen 14:24)
wherever you find the words of R' Eliezer son of R' Yose HaGelili in aggada, make your ear like a funnel
'not because you are more numerous... did the Lord desire you' (Deut 7:7): the Holy One said, I desire you, for even when I bestow greatness on you, you diminish yourselves before Me
I gave greatness to Abraham -- he said 'I am dust and ashes'; to Moses and Aaron -- 'what are we'; to David -- 'I am a worm and no man'
but the nations are not so: given greatness, Nimrod, Pharaoh, Sennacherib, Nebuchadnezzar and Hiram king of Tyre exalted themselves
greater is what is said of Moses and Aaron than of Abraham: of Abraham 'I am dust and ashes', of Moses and Aaron 'and what are we'
the world endures only for the sake of Moses and Aaron
written here 'and what [mah] are we', and written there 'He hangs the earth on nothing [beli-mah]' (Job 26:7)
R' Ila'a: the world endures only for one who restrains himself in a quarrel, as it says 'He hangs the earth on beli-mah'
R' Ila'a's verse: 'He hangs the earth on beli-mah' (Job 26:7)
R' Abbahu: [the world endures only] for one who makes himself as if he were not, as it says 'and beneath, the everlasting arms'
R' Abbahu's verse: 'and beneath, the everlasting arms' (Deut 33:27)
R' Yitzchak on Ps 58:2: what is a man's craft in this world? to make himself like a mute
might one think even for words of Torah? the verse says 'speak righteousness'
might he grow proud? the verse says 'judge the sons of men with equity'
R' Zeira: one may cover [the blood] with the dust of an idolatrous city
Ze'eiri: it is needed only for the dust of its dust [its ground]
as it is written 'gather all its spoil into its square and burn' (Deut 13:17): what lacks only gathering and burning -- excluding this, which lacks detaching, gathering and burning
Rava: mitzvot were not given for benefit
a shofar of idolatry -- one may not blow it; a lulav of idolatry -- one may not take it
if he blew [an idolatrous shofar] he has not fulfilled; if he took [an idolatrous lulav] he has not fulfilled
Rav Ashi: there [shofar, lulav] we require a measure, and idolatry is ground to powder in its measure
here, the more it is ground, the better for covering
